name: The Dolder Grand
positioning: Historic hotel on the hill above Zurich, around since 1899, pairing a castle-like main building with sleek glass wings, a 4,000-square-meter spa and an in-house art gallery
best_for: Travelers who plan their stay around a large spa
Art lovers who want views over Zurich, the lake and the mountains

facts.text: The hotel has been around since 1899.
Guests move from the castle-like main building into sleek dark gray-glass wings.
Rooms in the new wings have a sleeker feel, with chrome details and white leather.
Every Junior Suite Grand has a panoramic view of the city of Zurich, the lake and the Swiss mountains.
The Ladies' Spa and the Gentlemen's Spa each have a sauna, steam bath, foot bath, aroma pool, steam pots, plunge pool and solarium.
The spa's Aqua Zone has a swimming pool, whirlpools, a sanarium, a snow paradise, a steam bath and an outdoor sun terrace.
The spa has two private Spa Suites, each with a steam bath, whirlpool, balcony and fireplace.
A Chef's Table sits in the heart of the kitchen, where guests follow the creation of each dish.
Saltz restaurant has a patio and serves dishes like Zurich-style veal and rosti.
A traditional English Afternoon Tea is served in the lobby.
The hotel's weekly live music acts are a fixture in Zurich's music calendar.

highlights.text: The hotel has an art gallery with over 100 pieces from 90 artists, including Botero, Dali, Haring and Murakami.
A funicular beside the hotel runs down into the city center.
The spa has a meditation room with a dome made of mirror mosaic.
In the evening a DJ plays at the Canvas Bar, and bartenders mix signature drinks such as the Dolder Negroni.

considerations.text: The hotel sits up on the hill, not in the walkable heart of the city; guests use the valet car or the shuttle to get into Zurich.
Children are welcome in the spa from the age of twelve.
The hotel does not especially cater to kids, though families would not feel out of place.
